one_line: Trace failed manufacturing components to affected units and contain them with reversible oversight.
what_it_does: A quality-lineage simulator traces supplier lots through manufacturing relationships, compares containment scopes, previews notices, and stages auditable holds.
leverage_rationale: Structured lineage tools and shared state make precise, repeatable impact tracing materially safer than an agent scraping a complex quality UI.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes explicit relationships, evidence-scoped tools, corrected records, and reversible holds.
Video frames show the trace-failed-component workflow and populated dependency/result cards.
execution_rationale: The product presents a coherent investigation-to-containment workflow with strong domain-specific states; the video shows a consistent dashboard and populated trace results, though tool calls are not legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show a consistent 'Trace a failed component' interface progressing to related trace/dependency cards.
Packet specifies 312 affected units, containment comparisons, notices, audit trail, commit and undo.
impact_rationale: Manufacturing quality teams have a concrete high-stakes problem, and reducing both missed units and over-containment is directly valuable.
impact_evidence: Packet gives a specific supply-chain quality audience and a concrete failure scenario.
Claimed scenario distinguishes 312 affected units from 88 unrelated lookalike-lot units.
creativity_rationale: It is an original, deeply domain-specific application of agent-controlled lineage and human-approved containment, though the underlying quality workflow is established.
creativity_evidence: Combines evidence-scoped lineage tracing with containment-scope comparison and reversible approval.
The product frames show a focused supply-chain investigation model.
usability_note: The staged workflow and explanations appear usable, but text and exact interaction details are not fully legible in the frame sheet.
advance_reason: High impact and strong execution with a credible, meaningful WebMCP delta.

one_line: Turn a real OpenStreetMap view into AI map artwork without letting the model invent geography.
what_it_does: Locks map geometry, resolves features against OpenStreetMap, and stages a comparison between prompt-only and geography-grounded generated map imagery.
leverage_rationale: Page-owned map invariants and typed tools give the agent reliable geographic state that screenshot interpretation cannot provide comparably well.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes ten typed tools for focus, navigation, inspection, locking, feature marking, verification, and comparison staging.
Frames show a form-plus-map workflow with changing geographic views and selected fields.
execution_rationale: The concept and visual workflow are coherent, with map interaction and staged comparison visible; the final paid generation is intentionally not shown, limiting end-to-end proof.
execution_evidence: Frames show a consistent map/form UI progressing through geographic selections and map changes.
Packet reports six native calls with visible execution receipts and a deliberate stop before paid image generation.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real risk for people using AI-generated maps: plausible but false geography, while preserving creative use.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies map-grounding and false geographic relationships as the central problem.
New Orleans and Lower Manhattan examples provide concrete intended use.
creativity_rationale: The comparison of ungrounded versus source-locked map artwork is memorable and pursues a distinctive interaction model rather than merely adding chat to a map.
creativity_evidence: Uses the real place as an invariant source while letting AI interpret and style it.
Makes hallucinated geography visible through side-by-side comparison.
usability_note: The two-column map/form interaction is clear in frames, though generation completion is not shown.
red_flags: Paid image-generation result is not shown in the evidence.
advance_reason: Original concept with substantial leverage and credible audience value.

one_line: Publish human-readable digests and structured, expiring context patches for agents.
what_it_does: Publishes topic desks whose issues carry provenance, scope, confidence, validity windows, and explicit relationships to earlier claims.
leverage_rationale: Structured publication patches give agents scoped, provenance-bearing, expiring shared context rather than requiring ad hoc browsing and memory inference.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes typed agent context patches, claim provenance, scope, expiry, and replace/narrow/confirm/conflict relations.
Frames visibly show the publication UI and an 'Agent edition detected' panel.
execution_rationale: The publication model is unusually intentional and internally coherent; frames show a polished issue/agent-edition surface, but no clear tool execution receipt.
execution_evidence: Frames show a consistent dark publication interface with agent-edition detection and action controls.
Packet specifies scheduled desks, unchanged-packet suppression, locked patches, and provenance handling.
impact_rationale: There is a real need for keeping humans and agents current without silently turning publications into memory; the audience is broad enough and the use case concrete.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies stale assistants and post-question retrieval as the problem.
Topic desks cover model watch, food, wellbeing, culture, makers, and personal contacts.
creativity_rationale: Treating publication as a dual human-readable issue plus structured, expiring agent context is a fresh interaction and information model.
creativity_evidence: Explicit semantic relationships between claims are pursued as a core product primitive.
The 'publication does not silently equal memory' boundary is distinctive.
usability_note: The publication surface looks coherent, but the frame sheet does not prove the full patch approval flow.
red_flags: No legible tool invocation or completed patch application in frames.
advance_reason: High-concept information product with meaningful structured-agent leverage.

one_line: Dynamically turn settled paid APIs in a Stellar marketplace into callable WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Combines x402 payments, trust-ranked Bazaar listings, smart-wallet policies, and live dynamic tool registration for payable APIs.
leverage_rationale: The page dynamically derives callable tools from live marketplace settlement and trust data, making agent purchasing capability depend on structured payment state rather than UI scraping.
leverage_evidence: Packet says tools are registered from live Bazaar results with real settlement history and trust scores.
Packet describes payment-policy infrastructure, live endpoints, and dynamic tool creation without code changes.
execution_rationale: The architecture and product scope are ambitious and coherent, but demo_alive is unknown and the frames do not clearly prove a completed live payment/tool transaction.
execution_evidence: Frames show a marketplace/developer/agent control experience and settlement-oriented product surfaces.
Packet describes live Bazaar querying, facilitator settlement, and dynamic registration.
impact_rationale: Agents need a credible way to pay for APIs, and a trust-ranked marketplace with policy-governed spending addresses a concrete infrastructure gap.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies agent inability to pay as the core problem.
Includes real seller endpoints, settlement data, spending policies, and USDC flow.
creativity_rationale: Automatically converting real settlement-backed marketplace entries into WebMCP tools is a novel and ambitious agent-commerce interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Tool catalog is a live query result from economic activity rather than a build-time specification.
Combines marketplace trust, payment settlement, and browser-native tools.
usability_note: The marketplace concept is clear, but live flow and payment interaction are not fully evidenced.
red_flags: Demo availability is unknown; packet describes substantial pre-existing infrastructure.
No clear visible completed payment result.
standouts: Dynamic tool registration from settlement data
advance_reason: Potentially transformative WebMCP leverage and unusually ambitious infrastructure, tempered by verification gaps.

one_line: Recompose a plant catalog around a shopper's actual yard, constraints, and safety needs.
what_it_does: An agent describes a garden; the catalog deterministically ranks plants by light, salt, pets, irrigation, and other constraints with explained verdicts.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets an agent update live catalog state from conversational yard context, avoiding a rigid form while retaining deterministic, inspectable evaluation.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes describe_garden recomposing sections and shared page state.
Frames show an AI-assisted garden-center editor/site with visibly different rendered catalog states.
execution_rationale: The product has a coherent domain model, clear verdict explanations, and visible rendered iterations; frames show page composition but not every catalog result.
execution_evidence: Frames show consistent garden-center pages with a conversational editing panel and rendered green content sections.
Packet specifies verdicts, compromises, care routines, and what-would-change explanations.
impact_rationale: Plant shoppers have a concrete problem matching plants to real yards, pets, salt, water, and care capacity; the product offers actionable guidance.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies Southern Florida salt exposure and pet/toxicity concerns.
Deterministic suitability verdicts directly address shopper uncertainty.
creativity_rationale: The adaptive catalog and honest insufficient-data states are a fresh synthesis of conversational commerce and deterministic horticultural guidance.
creativity_evidence: Catalog recomposes around nuanced yard context rather than merely filtering cards.
Missing records are explicitly not treated as safety evidence.
usability_note: The conversational-to-visual adaptation is understandable, though the video frames emphasize editor states more than shopping completion.
advance_reason: Useful adaptive commerce experience with credible leverage and clear audience value.

one_line: Train and evaluate high-stakes delegation where agents stop at policy boundaries and humans decide trade-offs.
what_it_does: A deterministic crisis sandbox lets an agent inspect, forecast, simulate, and act within policy, then pauses before protected or over-risky actions for human approval.
leverage_rationale: Shared deterministic state, policy-bounded actions, and enforced human authority boundaries are central to the product and difficult to reproduce reliably by generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Packet specifies inspect/forecast/simulate/act tools with a protected decision queue.
Frames show the agent-safety control room, dependency graph, policy panels, and deterministic metrics.
execution_rationale: The central crisis workflow, policy constraints, pause boundary, and debrief are coherent and strongly evidenced by the product frames and specified state model.
execution_evidence: Frames show East Ring failure, coverage and cascade metrics, graph state, and policy-oriented controls.
Packet describes execution pausing at the first protected trade-off and recording the final debrief.
impact_rationale: Operations and security teams have a real need to test whether agents stop at the right authority boundary in consequential workflows.
impact_evidence: Packet names high-stakes operations, security, and delegation evaluation audiences.
Hospital-feed failure and protected-service trade-offs make the risk concrete.
creativity_rationale: A deterministic crisis-training environment that evaluates authority boundaries, not just task completion, is a memorable and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent optimization is explicitly separated from human decisions about what may be sacrificed.
Visible graph, policy, and outcome metrics support the concept deeply.
usability_note: The control-room framing is clear and stateful; small text limits direct inspection of every action label.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: transformative leverage, complete workflow evidence, high impact, and memorable originality.

one_line: Have an agent propose a fair feasible group-trip plan while unanimous human consent remains required.
what_it_does: Combines traveler constraints, deterministic validation, fairness breakdowns, reactive tools, and unanimous approval before immutable lock/export.
leverage_rationale: Reactive typed tools expose shared trip state and constraint validation, making agent proposals precise while keeping approval actions human-only.
leverage_evidence: Packet lists stateful tools with availability tied to setup, proposal, and unanimous approval.
Frames show populated trip-planning dashboards, itinerary cards, and total-cost summaries.
execution_rationale: The workflow has clear state transitions and deterministic validation; frames show populated planning and cost views, though the lock transition is not directly visible.
execution_evidence: Frames show trip configuration, traveler/itinerary cards, comparisons, and total trip cost.
Packet specifies budget, veto, capacity, schedule, transport, lodging, and location checks.
impact_rationale: Group travel planning has a clear audience and recurring coordination problem; fairness and feasibility checks directly address common failure modes.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies budget, must-have, veto, and preference conflicts among three travelers.
Human approval and read-only export support practical group coordination.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent constraint arithmetic, named fairness breakdowns, reactive tool availability, and unanimous consent is a fresh collaboration model.
creativity_evidence: Approval tools are deliberately withheld until all travelers consent.
Immutable locked allocation is a strong product-level consequence of the interaction design.
usability_note: The dashboard and summary views are legible and coherent; final unanimous-lock evidence is not shown.
red_flags: The decisive unanimous approval/lock state is described but not clearly visible in frames.
advance_reason: Strong practical collaboration design with meaningful WebMCP state and approval leverage.

one_line: Let agents investigate and propose decisions while consequential changes require explicit human approval.
what_it_does: A decision workspace stores options, evidence, criteria, contradictions, sensitivity analyses, scenarios, risks, pending proposals, and audit history.
leverage_rationale: The agent can operate on a live structured decision state and produce bounded proposals, while the product enforces a human approval gate for consequential changes.
leverage_evidence: Packet lists tools for evidence search, comparison, contradiction finding, sensitivity, scenarios, and risk.
Frames show ProofPilot's decision workspace and human-control feature sections.
execution_rationale: The workflow and safeguards are coherent and the UI is polished, but the frames do not show a completed agent analysis or approval transition end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Frames show consistent ProofPilot pages, human-control explanations, comparison content, and a recommendation form.
Packet specifies investigate → analyze → propose → approve → state change → audit trail.
impact_rationale: Teams making vendor, architecture, and other consequential choices need inspectable evidence and control over final decisions.
impact_evidence: Packet gives concrete decision audiences and names evidence disagreement, changing priorities, and authority as problems.
Human-approved state changes and audit trails directly address those risks.
creativity_rationale: The product turns agent reasoning into an interrogable, auditable decision process rather than a one-shot recommendation, a fresh and ambitious workspace model.
creativity_evidence: Explicit pending proposals and approval boundaries structure agent/human collaboration.
Interrogation of recommendations and 'what would change it' are central interaction elements.
usability_note: The workspace and safeguards are clearly presented, though the evidence is more landing/workspace-oriented than full execution proof.
red_flags: No clearly visible completed analysis or approved state change in frames.
standouts: Evidence and sensitivity analysis are first-class
advance_reason: High-value decision workflow with credible impact and substantial structured-agent leverage.

one_line: Edit video by editing words with a human and agent sharing one transcript-first editor.
what_it_does: A browser editor supports transcript cuts, transcription fixes, compositions, captions, timed overlays, background removal, and MP4 export through shared actions.
leverage_rationale: A transcript/timeline editor exposes narrow typed verbs over shared media state, making language-shaped editing substantially more precise than generic visual UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes 47 WebMCP tools backed by the same Zustand action hub as human controls.
Frames show a browser editor, console-like execution area, agent panel, and rendered page/product surfaces.
execution_rationale: The architecture and scope are coherent, but the frame sheet does not clearly show a completed edit/export result or legible tool invocation.
execution_evidence: Packet specifies transcript words with timestamps, compositions, overlays, captions, ML background removal, and export.
Frames show an editor/demo environment with persistent control and execution panels.
impact_rationale: Podcast and video creators have a real need for faster transcript-based editing, and shared human-agent state could reduce repetitive editing work.
impact_evidence: Packet targets talk-heavy video/podcast workflows and describes concrete editing operations.
Transcript-first editing is aligned with the stated creator workflow.
creativity_rationale: Treating an agent as a native language-shaped editor operating on the same undo stack is a strong and memorable synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Human buttons and agent tools share one narrow-verb action hub.
The concept extends transcript editing into live human/agent co-editing.
usability_note: The shared-editor idea is clear, but the frames are low-resolution and do not prove the export path.
red_flags: No legible end-to-end edit/export result in the viewed frames.
advance_reason: Creative, useful editor concept with meaningful agent leverage, though execution evidence is thinner than the top packets.

one_line: Give browser agents structured read-only access to a Nigerian marketplace for search, comparison, and purchase planning.
what_it_does: Exposes tools to search products, discover local stores, compare products, and prepare a purchase plan using marketplace data while leaving checkout to humans.
leverage_rationale: Typed marketplace search and comparison reduce scraping ambiguity and improve structured retrieval, but the same planning outcome remains possible through ordinary browsing with friction.
leverage_evidence: Packet lists four read-only tools returning product, price, stock, seller, and review data.
Frames show a green-and-white Co-Pilot interface with proposed plan cards, but no clear tool trace.
execution_rationale: The described product has a plausible narrow workflow, but the submission packaging is extremely thin and the frames do not clearly demonstrate a completed marketplace result.
execution_evidence: Frames show a Co-Pilot-like interface and generated response/plan cards, but text is blurred.
Packet describes manual fallback and shared search/purchase-planning logic.
impact_rationale: Local marketplace discovery and comparison can be valuable to Nigerian shoppers, especially where structured inventory and store information are hard to navigate.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies a real Nigerian marketplace and concrete shopper tasks.
Human-only checkout and seller messaging limit risk while preserving planning value.
creativity_rationale: Structured agent shopping on a marketplace is a useful implementation but largely a known category with limited novel interaction beyond the WebMCP surface.
creativity_evidence: Read-only search, store discovery, comparison, and purchase planning are coherent.
The frame sheet shows a conventional assistant/planning presentation.
usability_note: The intended flow is simple, but the actual product text and marketplace result details are not legible in the evidence.
red_flags: Devpost pitch and about text are inconsistent and contain substantial low-quality filler.
No clearly legible marketplace results or invocation evidence.
advance_reason: Plausible utility, but weak and unclear evidence plus limited novelty prevents confident advancement.
